q: Which AWS service extracts sentiment, key phrases and named entities from customer reviews without building a model?
e: Comprehend is the managed natural language processing service: sentiment, entities, key phrases, language detection, PII detection and custom classification.

q: A company wants to detect objects, faces and unsafe content in images and videos. Which service fits?
e: Rekognition analyses images and video: labels, faces, text in images and content moderation.

q: An insurer wants to pull text, form fields and tables out of scanned claim documents. Which service fits?
e: Textract goes beyond plain OCR: it extracts printed and handwritten text plus forms (key-value pairs) and tables.
an: Your Screenshot Inbox, where Oracle reads the text off a shared image, does Textract's job inside RPGACE.

q: A call centre needs to turn recorded phone calls into text. Which service fits?
e: Transcribe converts speech to text (automatic speech recognition). Polly does the opposite.

q: Which service turns written text into lifelike speech?
e: Polly is text-to-speech. Transcribe is speech-to-text.

q: Which service builds conversational chatbots with voice and text, using the same technology as Alexa?
e: Lex builds conversational interfaces (intents, slots) for voice and text bots.

q: Which service provides intelligent search across company documents, answering natural-language questions?
e: Kendra is ML-powered enterprise search. It can also act as a retriever for RAG.

q: An online shop wants real-time product recommendations for each user based on their behaviour. Which service fits?
e: Personalize builds recommendation systems using the same technology as Amazon.com, with no ML expertise needed.

q: Which service translates text between languages?
e: Translate is neural machine translation.

q: A model's low-confidence predictions need to be checked by people before being used. Which AWS service adds this human review step?
e: Amazon A2I builds human review workflows for ML predictions, for example when confidence falls below a threshold.
an: Same idea as RPGACE's Review queue: AI-generated jargon terms stay pending until you Accept or Reject each one.

q: Which type of neural network is traditionally best suited to image recognition?
e: CNNs detect visual patterns such as edges and shapes. Transformers are now also used for vision, but CNNs are the classic answer.

q: Which field of AI focuses on understanding and generating human language?
e: NLP covers text tasks: sentiment, translation, summarisation and question answering.

q: What is inference in machine learning?
o: Training a model on labelled data
Using a trained model to make predictions on new data
e: Inference is the 'use' phase: the trained model receives new input and returns a prediction.

q: A model must score each customer's whole history once a night, and nobody waits for the results. Which inference option is most cost-effective?
e: Batch inference processes large datasets offline. No always-on endpoint is needed, so it is cheaper for scheduled jobs.

q: A mobile app needs a prediction back in milliseconds every time a user taps a button. Which inference option fits?
e: Real-time endpoints serve low-latency, request-by-request predictions.

q: Requests have large payloads and can take several minutes to process, and the caller can collect the result later. Which SageMaker inference option fits?
e: Asynchronous inference queues requests, handles large payloads and long processing times, and can scale to zero when idle.
an: Like Bookworm: the first insight comes back fast, then the rest of the chapter finishes in the background and you check back later.

q: Traffic to a model is unpredictable with long idle periods, and some cold-start delay is acceptable. Which option keeps costs lowest?
e: Serverless inference scales automatically and costs nothing while idle.
an: RPGACE's Vercel functions work this way: nothing runs or costs between your requests.

q: Which describes semi-supervised learning?
o: Using a small amount of labelled data together with a large amount of unlabelled data
Grouping data with no labels at all
e: Semi-supervised learning combines a few labels with lots of unlabelled data. Useful when labelling is expensive.

q: Which is an example of anomaly detection?
o: Flagging a credit card purchase that is very unusual for that customer
e: Anomaly detection spots rare events that differ from normal patterns, such as fraud or equipment faults.

q: Which is a structured data source?
o: A database table of orders with fixed columns
A set of social media photos
e: Structured data has a fixed schema (rows and columns). Text, images and audio are unstructured.

q: What is a labelled dataset?
o: Data where each example has the correct answer attached
e: Labels are the target answers (spam or not spam, the price) that supervised learning trains on.

q: A model's features are missing for most records, so its predictions are poor. What does this show?
o: Model quality depends on data quality: garbage in, garbage out
The learning rate is too low
e: No algorithm fixes missing or poor data. Data collection and preparation usually matter more than model choice.
an: RPGACE's beat matching: the scoring code exists, but scale and genre are filled in on 0 of 32 reference tracks, so matches always come out the same.

q: Why do teams use a validation set during training?
o: To tune hyperparameters and compare models without touching the test set
e: Validation data guides tuning choices. Keeping the test set separate gives an honest final score.

q: Which technique helps reduce overfitting?
o: Using more varied training data and regularisation
Training for many more epochs on the same small data
e: More diverse data, regularisation, early stopping and simpler models all help a model generalise.

q: What does exploratory data analysis (EDA) involve?
o: Looking at statistics and charts of the data to understand it before modelling
e: EDA (distributions, correlations, missing values) happens early in the lifecycle to understand the data.

q: Which business metric best shows whether a new recommendation model was worth building?
o: Increase in revenue per customer after launch
Number of layers in the network
e: Technical metrics show model quality. Business metrics such as revenue, conversion, cost saved and customer satisfaction show value.

q: Which AWS service lets you choose from a hub of pre-trained models and deploy them with a few clicks inside SageMaker?
e: JumpStart offers pre-trained and foundation models, plus solution templates, ready to deploy or fine-tune.

q: Which describes transfer learning?
o: Reusing a model trained on one task as the starting point for a related task
Training a model from random weights only
Exporting a model to a different file format
e: Transfer learning reuses learned knowledge, so you need much less data and compute. Fine-tuning a foundation model is a form of it.

q: Which is an example of a computer vision use case?
o: Checking products on a factory line for visible defects
e: Computer vision interprets images and video, for example quality inspection, face detection and medical imaging.

q: Which ML approach is used to predict demand for the next 12 weeks from past weekly sales?
e: Forecasting predicts future values from ordered historical data.
